title: Propp — Functions of Dramatis Personae
source: Vladimir Propp, Morphology of the Folktale (1928)
license: system/idea (not copyrightable); descriptions authored for monomyth
tier_note: The 31-function system + symbols are freely modelable. This is the engine's core generative grammar: functions occur in a fixed relative order; any tale selects a subset. Symbols follow Propp's standard notation.

preparatory.name: Initial Situation
preparatory.description: The members of a family or the hero are introduced; the setting is established. Not a function proper, but the ground the functions act on.

items.name: Absentation
items.description: A member of the family absents themselves from home (the elder leaves, dies, or the hero departs).

items.name: Interdiction
items.description: An interdiction or prohibition is addressed to the hero (“do not go there”, “do not do X”).

items.name: Violation
items.description: The interdiction is violated. A new personage, the villain, enters the tale.

items.name: Reconnaissance
items.description: The villain makes an attempt at reconnaissance, seeking information about the victim.

items.name: Delivery
items.description: The villain receives information about the victim.

items.name: Trickery
items.description: The villain attempts to deceive the victim to take possession of them or their belongings.

items.name: Complicity
items.description: The victim is deceived and unwittingly helps the enemy.

items.name: Villainy or Lack
items.description: The villain causes harm/injury to a family member (A), OR a member lacks/desires something (a). This launches the plot.

items.name: Mediation
items.description: Misfortune or lack is made known; the hero is dispatched, approached with a request or command, allowed to go, or sent.

items.name: Beginning Counteraction
items.description: The seeker-hero agrees to or decides upon counteraction.

items.name: Departure
items.description: The hero leaves home.

items.name: First Function of the Donor
items.description: The hero is tested, interrogated, attacked, etc., preparing the way for receiving a magical agent or helper.

items.name: Hero's Reaction
items.description: The hero reacts to the actions of the future donor (passes/fails the test, frees a captive, etc.).

items.name: Receipt of a Magical Agent
items.description: The hero acquires the use of a magical agent (object, helper, ability, or knowledge).

items.name: Guidance
items.description: The hero is transferred, delivered, or led to the whereabouts of an object of search.

items.name: Struggle
items.description: The hero and villain join in direct combat or contest.

items.name: Branding
items.description: The hero is branded or marked (a wound, a token, a ring).

items.name: Victory
items.description: The villain is defeated.

items.name: Liquidation
items.description: The initial misfortune or lack is liquidated / resolved.

items.name: Return
items.description: The hero returns.

items.name: Pursuit
items.description: The hero is pursued.

items.name: Rescue
items.description: The hero is rescued from pursuit.

items.name: Unrecognized Arrival
items.description: The hero arrives home or in another country unrecognized.

items.name: Unfounded Claims
items.description: A false hero presents unfounded claims.

items.name: Difficult Task
items.description: A difficult task is proposed to the hero.

items.name: Solution
items.description: The task is resolved.

items.name: Recognition
items.description: The hero is recognized (by a mark, token, or accomplished task).

items.name: Exposure
items.description: The false hero or villain is exposed.

items.name: Transfiguration
items.description: The hero is given a new appearance (transfigured, healed, newly clothed).

items.name: Punishment
items.description: The villain or false hero is punished.

items.name: Wedding
items.description: The hero is married and/or ascends the throne — rewarded.
